title: adaptive anchor-KL / safety constraint -- CONFIRMATORY NEGATIVE (== anchor); KEEP mechanism
source_commit_cited: 96f35f7 (R6: no gate operating point beats the anchor; optimal anchor-deviation=0)
decision: KEEP the mechanism (adaptive controller load-bearing + stable); CONFIRMATORY NEGATIVE on the deployed gain -- adaptive anchor-KL residual == anchor exactly (edit_rate 0, retention 1.0, CI[0,0]); the fixed anchor protection was NOT the reason R3/R6 == anchor.

anchor_kl_term.def: mean sigmoid(z) over candidate edges (deviation from flip-nothing anchor)

adaptive_beta_controller.law: retention<target -> beta*1.5; retention>=target & val-improve -> beta*0.7; clamp [0,10]

r3_ppo_critic_entropy_rawl2.note: one variable = the anchor pull, fixed->adaptive

deployable.eval_decode: MAP decode (flip iff z>0) via residual_decode_from_flips -- 0 evaluator calls
deployable.csi_scope: current-frame channel (stale overlay off, as R3/R5/R6); stale-overlay-on full pilot is R8

result_5seed.config: 20 epochs, ppo_epochs 4, 6 train scenes, seeds [0-4]; arms fixed(residual_prior=-1.0) vs adaptive(residual_prior=0.0 + adaptive anchor-KL)

interpretation: The adaptive anchor-KL controller is load-bearing (beta_anchor tightens AND loosens per seed, distinct trajectories, never diverges) but the residual policy lands EXACTLY at the anchor (edit_rate 0, retention 1.0) -- even with the fixed pull removed (residual_prior=0) and the trust region loosened, the PPO advantage provides no beneficial-direction gradient, so there is nothing to deviate toward. Confirms the fixed anchor protection was NOT the cause of R3/R6 == anchor; the binding limit is the deployable direction signal (R6 precision limit). Three independent mechanisms (R3 fixed-prior PPO, R6 evidence gate, R7 adaptive KL) all land at the anchor.
effect_on_decision: changes the actor loss + training dynamics (beta adapts) but NOT the deployed topology (== anchor, edit_rate 0 all seeds) -- null effect on the action, reported honestly.
